title: Does the benefit of TEER in secondary MR vary by baseline risk and over time? A reconstructed-IPD meta-analysis of the randomised trials

pico.population: Patients with heart failure and moderate to severe or severe secondary MR on guideline-directed medical therapy
pico.outcomes: Death, heart failure hospitalisation, composite; time-varying hazards and competing risks

decision: Which patients with secondary MR should be offered TEER, and when in the heart failure trajectory
decision_maker: Heart failure and structural cardiologists, heart teams
why_now: Three randomised trials (PMIDs 30280640, 30145927, 39216092) point in different directions on the surface; no IPD-level pooled analysis appears in the appraised subset, and the 5-year COAPT follow-up (PMID 36876756) allows time-varying effects to be examined.

competing.note: ACHILLES-HF, TEER in HFrEF with secondary MR, not before 2030

designs.primary: Reconstructed-IPD meta-analysis from published Kaplan-Meier curves with one-stage Cox and flexible parametric models, treatment-covariate interaction using published subgroup data, landmark and restricted mean survival time analyses
designs.alternative: Two-stage aggregate meta-regression with Bayesian reanalysis of the trial results

data_required: Digitised Kaplan-Meier curves, numbers at risk, baseline characteristics from the three trials; trial-level covariates (MR severity, LV volume, medical therapy intensity)
data_sources: Trial investigators for any available IPD
feasibility: High for reconstruction (owner method); IPD sharing would raise credibility but is not required.
overlap: No overlap with listed active projects.

G1.note: Decision is common in heart failure practice and judged on death and heart failure hospitalisation (PMID 30280640, PMID 36876756).

G2.note: Guideline position is unverified because guideline extracts have not been retrieved; G2 is judged on trial evidence only. Trials conflict (PMID 30145927 versus PMID 30280640) and no pooled individual-level analysis is in the subset.

G3.note: No adequately powered randomised trial of TEER versus medical therapy is listed to report within 24 months (earliest eligible primary completion 2030-09 for NCT07758023). A meta-analysis in a target or general journal in the past 24 months is not visible in the appraised subset, so this must be confirmed by the adversarial search before promotion.

G4.note: Reconstructed IPD can test time-varying effects and interaction that single trials could not; a guideline committee could cite it.

G5.note: Not a repeat aggregate meta-analysis, but it pools only three trials (derived total 1,423 patients from 614, 304 and 505), so the added value depends on the effect-modification findings.

impact.why: Secondary MR with heart failure is common and carries high mortality.

novelty.why: Pooling is intuitive, so a prior synthesis may exist outside the appraised subset.

equipoise.why: Benefit is shown in two of three randomised trials, but selection remains unresolved.

design.why: Reconstructed IPD is credible but limited by published data.

timeliness.why: The 2024 trials are recent and no further trial reads out before 2030.

citation.why: Pooled analyses of landmark trials are cited moderately in the target journals.

next_actions: Search PROSPERO and the full store for an existing IPD or reconstructed-IPD synthesis
Extract curves and numbers at risk for the three trials
Register the protocol on PROSPERO with pre-specified interaction analyses

title: Target trial emulation of TEER versus medical therapy in secondary MR patients outside the COAPT criteria

pico.population: Patients with heart failure and moderate to severe secondary MR who would not meet trial eligibility (for example advanced LV dilatation, severe pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction)
pico.outcomes: All-cause death, heart failure hospitalisation, health status
pico.timing: Time zero at the first echocardiogram meeting criteria; 3 years

decision: Whether TEER should be offered to patients excluded from the randomised trials
decision_maker: Heart teams, heart failure clinicians, commissioners
why_now: Registry analyses show worse outcomes in trial-ineligible patients (PMID 38267110: death or HFH HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.57 to 1.91; PMID 34886961) without a medical-therapy comparator; a transportability analysis (PMID 42233929) addresses only trial-eligible patients.

competing.note: ACHILLES-HF, HFrEF; eligibility unspecified in the file

designs.primary: Target trial emulation using linked national heart failure, echocardiography and procedure data with clone-censor-weight handling of the grace period and inverse probability weighting
designs.alternative: Bayesian transport of COAPT effect estimates to the ineligible population with explicit assumptions

data_required: Population-level echocardiography with MR grade and LV dimensions, linked hospital and mortality data, medication records, TEER procedure codes
data_sources: National linked echocardiography and hospital data
feasibility: Moderate to low; needs a linked echocardiography source and a collaborator with TEER-treated and untreated cohorts.
overlap: No overlap with listed active projects.

G1.note: Common decision in heart failure with outcomes judged on death and heart failure hospitalisation (PMID 38267110).

G2.note: Guideline position is unverified because guideline extracts have not been retrieved; G2 is judged on trial evidence only. No randomised evidence exists in the ineligible population in the trials file.

G3.note: Listed trials report in 2030 or later and are not framed around ineligible patients.

G4.note: Target trial emulation with a credible untreated comparator; a stated reason: registry-only designs without untreated patients cannot estimate the effect, and randomisation in this group is unlikely to be funded.

G5.note: Not a single-centre series or subgroup analysis; it needs a national linked dataset.

impact.why: Trial-ineligible patients are 44.3% of 6,675 treated functional MR patients in PMID 38267110.

novelty.why: No comparative estimate in ineligible patients is in the subset.

equipoise.why: Benefit in ineligible patients is genuinely unknown.

design.why: Confounding by indication and immortal time are serious and depend on data richness.

timeliness.why: Registry and transportability publications are accumulating, with no trial due before 2030.

citation.why: Emulation papers on excluded populations reach target journals.

feasibility.why: The required linked echocardiography and untreated cohorts are not currently held by the owner.

next_actions: Identify a national echocardiography-linked dataset and a collaborator
Specify the target trial protocol and eligibility mapping to COAPT criteria
Run a feasibility count of untreated eligible patients

title: Target trial emulation of TEER versus no mitral intervention in cardiogenic shock with severe MR

pico.population: Adults in cardiogenic shock with severe MR
pico.intervention: TEER within a defined window after shock onset
pico.comparator: No mitral intervention (medical and mechanical support only)
pico.outcomes: 30-day and 1-year all-cause death, recurrent shock, heart failure hospitalisation
pico.timing: Time zero at shock diagnosis with MR confirmation

decision: Whether to proceed to TEER during shock with severe MR
why_now: PMID 36126766 (3,797 patients) associates device success with lower mortality but conditions on a post-baseline success measure; PMID 34463727 compares interventions with conservative care after infarction with confounding.

competing.note: EMCAMI, early TEER after myocardial infarction; shock status not stated in the file

designs.primary: Target trial emulation with clone-censor-weight treatment of waiting time and device success excluded from baseline
designs.alternative: Individual-patient pooled cohort analysis across shock registries

data_required: Shock registry data with echocardiographic MR grade, haemodynamics, support devices and mitral procedure indicators
feasibility: Uncertain; registries may not record MR grade or mitral procedures, and numbers treated are small.
overlap: Overlaps the owner's state-of-the-art review of acute MR and cardiogenic shock; this is an original study, not a duplicate, but should be coordinated.

G2.note: Guideline position is unverified because guideline extracts have not been retrieved; G2 is judged on trial evidence only. Only observational comparisons exist.

G3.note: The one listed trial (NCT06282042, 250 participants, 2027-06-16) is not stated to include shock, but it could still affect the question and must be checked.

G4.note: Data adequacy is unresolved: a credible emulation needs MR grade and mitral procedure fields that the owner's registries may lack; the gate cannot be passed until a dataset is confirmed.

G5.note: Not a surrogate-only or small-series design if adequate data are found.

impact.why: Severe MR in shock is uncommon, but mortality is very high.

novelty.why: No comparison with untreated patients is in the subset.

equipoise.why: Observational data suffer survivor bias, so equipoise is real.

design.why: Small samples and missing variables limit credibility.

timeliness.why: Interest in shock systems is high, with one trial reporting in 2027.

citation.why: Shock papers are well cited but the population is niche.

feasibility.why: Owner holds shock registry routes, but mitral fields are uncertain.

next_actions: Check the data dictionaries of BCIS and ICNARC for MR and mitral procedure fields
Agree scope with the acute MR and shock review authors

title: Value of information for early intervention in asymptomatic severe degenerative MR

pico.population: Asymptomatic adults with severe degenerative MR and preserved LV function
pico.comparator: Watchful waiting with intervention on symptoms or LV triggers
pico.outcomes: Cardiovascular death, heart failure, quality-adjusted life years, costs

decision: Whether to refer asymptomatic patients for early repair and whether further trials are warranted
decision_maker: Cardiologists, heart teams, guideline committees, funders
why_now: Observational evidence favours early surgery (PMID 40799133: cardiovascular death HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.40) but is single-centre; one randomised trial (NCT03389542, 424 participants) is not due until 2033, so a model can size what that trial and others can resolve.

competing.note: REVERSE-MR, early repair versus watchful waiting
INTEGRATE, cardiac magnetic resonance in surgical decisions
MARCER, TEER in exercise-induced severe MR

designs.primary: Patient-level Markov microsimulation with probabilistic sensitivity analysis and expected value of sample information
designs.alternative: Bayesian evidence synthesis of observational and randomised data feeding a trial design simulation

data_required: Natural history and surgical outcome parameters from published cohorts, costs and utilities from national sources
feasibility: High; matches the owner's microsimulation and VOI methods.
overlap: No overlap with listed active projects.

G1.note: Common decision, judged on cardiovascular death and heart failure.

G2.note: Guideline position is unverified because guideline extracts have not been retrieved; G2 is judged on trial evidence only. The only randomised evidence is not yet reported.

G3.note: The one listed adequately sized randomised trial completes in 2033, beyond 24 months.

G4.note: VOI is the stated reason: it quantifies whether a trial is justified; a weaker design would not size the uncertainty.

G5.note: Not a repeat meta-analysis or surrogate-only study; it depends on the model parameters being credible.

impact.why: Asymptomatic severe MR is a large patient group.

novelty.why: A VOI analysis for this decision is not in the subset.

equipoise.why: Observational data favour early repair, randomised data are pending.

design.why: A model is only as strong as its inputs, which are largely observational.

citation.why: Decision models in the target journals are cited moderately.

feasibility.why: Direct fit to the owner's skills.

next_actions: Extract natural history and surgical outcome inputs from the stored records
Draft a PROSPERO-style protocol for the input synthesis

title: Pre-registered synthesis of randomised TEER versus surgery trials in primary MR, timed to the readouts

pico.population: Adults with severe primary MR and elevated surgical risk or older age
pico.outcomes: Death, heart failure hospitalisation, MR recurrence, reintervention

decision: Choice of TEER or surgery in primary MR
why_now: Observational comparison exists (PMID 38243821) and earlier trial follow-up is old (PMID 26718672: 5-year results for the first randomised comparison); several randomised trials are registered.

designs.primary: Prospectively registered meta-analysis with a pre-specified update at each readout, random-effects REML with Hartung-Knapp adjustment
designs.alternative: Reconstructed-IPD synthesis once the trials publish

feasibility: High; uses the owner's same-day workflow.
overlap: Fits the owner's same-day congress SRMA workflow; no overlap with listed projects.

G1.note: Common decision judged on hard outcomes.

G2.note: Guideline position is unverified because guideline extracts have not been retrieved; G2 is judged on trial evidence only. Randomised evidence in primary MR is limited in the subset.

G3.note: Adequately sized randomised trials of the same comparison are listed to report within 24 months (NCT03271762 in 2026-12, NCT04198870 in 2027-12), so the question will be answered by the trials themselves; the value lies only in a timely pooled analysis.

G4.note: A pre-specified update gives a guideline-citable synthesis.

G5.note: Pooling a few trials after they report risks being an incremental repeat unless IPD or new analyses are added.

impact.why: Primary MR is common and the decision frequent.

novelty.why: The synthesis follows the trials rather than preceding them.

design.why: Pre-registration is sound but each trial may be small.

citation.why: Timed syntheses attract attention when published at the readout.

next_actions: Register the protocol before the first readout
Confirm comparators and primary outcomes from the trial publications when available
Pre-position the analysis code with a rerun function
